verses.text: Woe to dem wey go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust for chariots because dem plenty, and for horsemen because dem very strong, but dem no look to di Holy One of Israel, neither dem seek di Lord!
Yet e too dey wise, and e go bring disaster, and no go call back im words, but go rise up against di house of evildoers, and against di help of dem wey work iniquity.

Now di Egyptians na men, and no be God. Dem horses na flesh, and no be spirit. When di Lord stretch out im hand, both di helper go stumble, and im wey dey helped go fall, and dem all go perish together.

Because di Lord talk to me like dis: “As di lion and di young lion growling over im prey, wey when multitude of shepherds dey called out against am, e no dey dismayed at dem voice, nor abase imself for dem noise, so di Lord of Armies go come down to fight for Mount Zion and for im hill.
As birds hovering, so di Lord of Armies go defend Jerusalem. By defending, e go also deliver am. By passing over, e go preserve am.”
Return to am from whom una don deeply revolted, una children of Israel.
Because for dat day everyone go cast away im idols of silver and im idols of gold, wey una own hands don make for una as sin.
“Di Assyrian go fall by di sword, no of man. Sword, no of men, go devour am. E go flee from di sword, and im young men go dey put to forced labour.
Im rock go pass away by reason of terror, and im princes go dey dismayed at di banner,” talk di Lord, wey im fire dey Zion, and im furnace for Jerusalem.
See, king go reign in righteousness, and princes go rule in justice.
Man go be like hiding place from di wind, and shelter from di storm, like streams of water for dry place, like di shade of great rock for weary land.
Di eyes of dem wey see no go dey dim, and di ears of dem wey hear go listen.
Di heart of di rash go understand knowledge, and di tongue of di stammerers go dey ready to speak plainly.
Di fool no go dey called noble again, nor di scoundrel dey said to be gracious.

Because di fool go speak folly, and im heart go work iniquity, to practice ungodliness, and to utter error against di Lord, to make di soul of di hungry empty, and to cause di drink of di thirsty to fail.
Di weapons of di scoundrel dey evil. E devise wicked plans to destroy di humble with lying words, even when di needy speak right.
But di noble devise noble things, and for noble things e go stand.
Rise up, una women wey dey at ease, hear my voice. Una careless daughters, give ear to my speech.
After one year and some days una go dey troubled, una careless women, because di vintage go fail, di harvest no go come.
Tremble, una women wey dey at ease. Dey troubled, una careless ones. Strip, make una bare, and gird sackcloth on una waist.
Dem go beat dem breasts for di pleasant fields, for di fruitful vine.
For di land of my people thorns and briers go come up, yes, for all di joyous houses for di joyous city.
Because di palace go dey forsaken. Di populous city go dey deserted. Di hill and di watchtower go be dens forever, joy of wild donkeys, pasture of flocks;
until di Spirit dey poured on us from on high, and di wilderness become fruitful field, and di fruitful field dey regarded as forest.
Den justice go dwell for di wilderness, and righteousness go remain for di fruitful field.
Di work of righteousness go be peace, and di effect of righteousness quietness and confidence forever.
My people go dwell for peaceful habitation, for secure dwellings and for quiet resting places.
But hail go come down on di forest, and di city go dey utterly laid low.
Blessed na una wey sow beside all waters, wey send out freely di ox and di donkey.

Woe to you wey destroy, though dem no destroy you, and deal treacherously, though dem no deal treacherously with you! When you don finish destroying, dem go destroy you. When you don finish dealing treacherously, dem go deal treacherously with you.
Di Lord, show us grace. We don wait for you. Be our arm every morning, our salvation also for di time of trouble.
At di noise of di tumult, di peoples don flee. When you lift yourself up, di nations don scatter.
Your plunder go dey gathered as caterpillar gather. As locusts dey leap, people go leap on am.
Di Lord dey exalted, because e dwell on high. E don fill Zion with justice and righteousness.
E go be di stability of your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom and knowledge. Di fear of di Lord na im treasure.
See, dem brave ones cry outside. Di ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
Di highways dey waste. Di wayfaring man cease. E don break di covenant. E don despise di cities. E no regard man.
Di land mourn and languish. Lebanon dey ashamed and wither away. Sharon dey like desert, and Bashan and Carmel dey shake off dem leaves.
“Now I go rise,” talk di Lord. “Now I go lift myself up. Now I go dey exalted.
You go conceive chaff. You go bring forth stubble. Your breath na fire wey go devour you.
Di peoples go be like di burning of lime, like thorns wey dem cut down, wey dem burn for fire.”
Hear, una wey dey far off, wetin I don do! Una wey dey near, acknowledge my might!
Di sinners for Zion dey afraid. Trembling don seize di godless: “Who among us fit dwell with di devouring fire? Who among us fit dwell with everlasting burning?”

Di one wey waka righteously, and speak uprightly, di one wey despise di gain of oppressions, wey shake im hands so dem no hold bribe, wey stop im ears from hearing of blood, and shut im eyes from looking at evil,
e go dwell on high. Im place of defence go be di fortress of rocks. Im bread go dey given. Im water go dey sure.
Your eyes go see di king for im beauty. Dem go see land wey dey far off.
Your heart go meditate on terror: “Where di scribe dey? Where di one wey weigh tribute dey? Where di one wey count di towers dey?”
You no go see di fierce people again, di people of obscure speech wey you no fit understand, of stammering tongue wey you no fit comprehend.
Look upon Zion, di city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes go see Jerusalem, quiet habitation, tent wey no go dey moved, wey im stakes no go ever dey pulled up, neither any of im cords go break.
But dere di Lord go be mighty for us, place of broad rivers and streams, wey no galley with oars go go, neither gallant ship go pass.
Because di Lord na our judge. Di Lord na our lawgiver. Di Lord na our king. E go save us.
Your ropes dey loose. Dem no fit hold di mast firm, neither spread di sail. Den dem go divide di plunder of great spoil. Di lame go take di prey.
Di inhabitant no go talk say, “I dey sick.” Di people wey dwell inside am go dey forgiven dem iniquity.
Come near, una nations, to hear! Listen, una peoples! Make di earth hear, and all wey full inside am, di world, and all wey come out of am.
Because di Lord dey angry against all di nations, and fury against all dem army. E don utterly destroy dem. E don deliver dem to di slaughter.
Dem slain go dey cast out, and dem dead bodies go send up stench, and di mountains go melt with dem blood.
All di army of heaven go dissolve, and di skies go roll up like scroll. All dem army go fade away, as di leaf dey fade from di vine, and as fading leaf from di fig tree.
For my sword don drink well for heaven. See, e go come down on Edom, and on di people of my curse, for judgment.

Di sword of di Lord don full with blood. E don dey made greasy with fat, with di blood of lambs and goats, with di fat of di kidneys of rams. Because di Lord get sacrifice for Bozrah, and great slaughter for di land of Edom.
Di wild oxen go come down with dem, and di young bulls with di mighty bulls. Dem land go dey drunk with blood, and dem dust made greasy with fat.
Because na di day of di Lord vengeance, year of recompense for di cause of Zion.
Im streams go turn to pitch, and im dust to sulfur, and im land go become burning pitch.
E no go dey quenched night or day. Im smoke go go up forever. From generation to generation e go lie waste. None go pass through am forever and ever.
But di pelican and di porcupine go possess am. Di owl and di raven go dwell inside am. E go stretch over am di line of confusion, and di plumb line of emptiness.
Dem nobles no go dey dere to call di kingdom, and all im princes go be nothing.
Thorns go come up for im palaces, nettles and thistles for im fortresses. E go be habitation of jackals, court for ostriches.
Di wild animals of di desert go meet di wolves, and di wild goat go cry to im fellow. Yes, di night creature go settle dere, and find for imself place of rest.
Di owl go make im nest dere, and lay, and hatch, and gather im young under im shade. Yes, di kites go gather dere, every one with im mate.
Seek from di book of di Lord, and read: no one of dem go dey missing. None go lack im mate. Because my mouth don command, and im Spirit don gather dem.
E don cast di lot for dem, and im hand don divide am to dem by line. Dem go possess am forever. From generation to generation dem go dwell inside am.
Di wilderness and di dry land go dey glad. Di desert go rejoice and blossom like di rose.
E go blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Di glory of Lebanon go dey given to am, di excellency of Carmel and Sharon. Dem go see di glory of di Lord, di excellency of our God.
Strengthen di weak hands, and make di feeble knees firm.
Talk to dem wey get fearful heart, “Dey strong! No fear! See, your God go come with vengeance, God with recompense. E go come and save you.”
Den di eyes of di blind go open, and di ears of di deaf go dey unstopped.
Den di lame man go leap like deer, and di tongue of di mute go sing. Because waters go break out for di wilderness, and streams for di desert.
Di burning sand go become pool, and di thirsty ground springs of water. For di habitation of jackals, where dem lie down, grass go grow with reeds and rushes.
Highway go dey dere, and way, and e go dey called di Way of Holiness. Di unclean no go pass over am, but e go be for dem. Di wayfaring men, even fools, no go go astray inside am.
No lion go dey dere, neither any ravenous animal go go up on am. Dem no go dey found dere, but di redeemed go waka dere.
Di ransomed of di Lord go return, and come with singing to Zion, with everlasting joy on dem heads. Dem go obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing go flee away.
Now for di fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all di fortified cities of Judah, and capture dem.
Di king of Assyria send Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with great army. E stand by di conduit of di upper pool, for di highway of di fuller field.
Den Eliakim, Hilkiah pikin, wey dey over di household, and Shebna di scribe, and Joah, Asaph pikin, di recorder, come out to am.
Rabshakeh talk to dem, “Tell Hezekiah, ‘Di great king, di king of Assyria, talk like dis: Wetin be dis confidence wey you dey trust?
You talk (but na only vain words) say, “I get counsel and strength for war.” Now who you dey trust, say you don rebel against me?
See, you dey trust for di staff of dis broken reed, even Egypt. If man lean on am, e go go inside im hand and pierce am. So be Pharaoh king of Egypt to all wey trust am.
But if you talk to me, “We trust for di Lord our God,” no be di one wey Hezekiah don take im high places and im altars away, and talk to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘Una must worship before dis altar’?
Now therefore, make pledge, I beg, to my master di king of Assyria, and I go give you 2,000 horses, if you fit set riders on dem.
How den you go turn back di face of one governor, of di least of my master servants, and put your trust for Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Now I don come up without di Lord against dis land to destroy am? Di Lord talk to me, “Go up against dis land, and destroy am.”’”

Den Eliakim, Shebna and Joah talk to Rabshakeh, “Speak to your servants in Aramaic, I beg you, because we understand am. No speak to us for di Jews language, for di ears of di people wey dey on di wall.”
But Rabshakeh talk, “My master send me to your master and to you to speak dis words? No be to di men wey sit on di wall, to eat dem own dung and drink dem own urine with una?”
Den Rabshakeh stand, and cry with loud voice for di Jews language, and talk, “Hear di words of di great king, di king of Assyria.
Di king talk like dis: ‘No make Hezekiah deceive una, because e no go fit deliver una.
No make Hezekiah make una trust for di Lord, say, “Di Lord go surely deliver us. Dis city no go dey given into di hand of di king of Assyria.”

No listen to Hezekiah, because di king of Assyria talk like dis: “Make peace with me, and come out to me. Make every one of una eat of im vine, and every one of im fig tree, and drink every one water of im own cistern,
until I come and take una away to land like una own land, land of grain and new wine, land of bread and vineyards.
Beware lest Hezekiah persuade una, say, ‘Di Lord go deliver us.’ Any of di gods of di nations don deliver im land out of di hand of di king of Assyria?
Where di gods of Hamath and Arpad dey? Where di gods of Sepharvaim dey? And dem don deliver Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all di gods of dis lands don deliver dem land out of my hand, say di Lord go deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?”’”
But dem keep quiet, and answer am no word, because di king commandment na, “No answer am.”
Den Eliakim, Hilkiah pikin, wey dey over di household, and Shebna di scribe, and Joah, Asaph pikin, di recorder, come to Hezekiah with dem clothes torn, and tell am di words of Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah hear am, e tear im clothes, cover imself with sackcloth, and enter di house of di Lord.
E send Eliakim, wey dey over di household, and Shebna di scribe, and di elders of di priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah di prophet, Amoz pikin.
Dem talk to am, “Hezekiah talk like dis: ‘Dis day na day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of disgrace, because children don reach di moment of birth, and no strength dey to deliver.

Maybe di Lord your God go hear di words of Rabshakeh, wey im master di king of Assyria don send to defy di living God, and go rebuke di words wey di Lord your God don hear. Therefore lift up prayer for di remnant wey dey left.’”
So di servants of King Hezekiah come to Isaiah.
Isaiah talk to dem, “Tell your master, ‘Di Lord talk like dis: No dey afraid because of di words wey you don hear, wey di servants of di king of Assyria don use blaspheme me.
See, I go put spirit inside am, and e go hear rumour, and return to im own land. I go cause am to fall by di sword for im own land.’”
So Rabshakeh return, and find di king of Assyria dey fight against Libnah, because e don hear say e don leave Lachish.
E hear say about Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “E don come out to fight against you.” When e hear am, e send messengers to Hezekiah, say,
“Tell Hezekiah king of Judah like dis: ‘No make your God, wey you dey trust, deceive you, say, “Jerusalem no go dey given into di hand of di king of Assyria.”
See, you don hear wetin di kings of Assyria don do to all di lands, destroying dem utterly. Una go dey delivered?
Di gods of di nations don deliver dem wey my fathers destroy, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and di children of Eden wey dey Telassar?
Where di king of Hamath dey, and di king of Arpad, and di king of di city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?’”
Hezekiah receive di letter from di hand of di messengers, and read am. Hezekiah go up to di house of di Lord, and spread am before di Lord.
Hezekiah pray to di Lord, say,
“Di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, wey sit above di cherubim, you na God, even you alone, of all di kingdoms of di earth. You don make heaven and earth.
Di Lord, bend your ear, and hear. Di Lord, open your eyes, and see. Hear all di words of Sennacherib, wey e don send to defy di living God.
Truly, di Lord, di kings of Assyria don lay waste all di countries and dem land,
and don cast dem gods into di fire, because dem no be gods, but di work of men hands, wood and stone. Therefore dem don destroy dem.
Now therefore, di Lord our God, save us from im hand, so that all di kingdoms of di earth go know say you alone na di Lord.”
Den Isaiah, Amoz pikin, send to Hezekiah, say, “Di Lord, di God of Israel, talk like dis: ‘Because you don pray to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria,
dis na di word wey di Lord don speak concerning am: “Di virgin daughter of Zion don despise you and laugh you to scorn. Di daughter of Jerusalem don shake her head behind you.
Who you don defy and blaspheme? Against who you don raise your voice and lift your eyes on high? Against di Holy One of Israel!

By your servants you don defy di Lord, and don talk, ‘With di multitude of my chariots I don come up to di height of di mountains, to di far recesses of Lebanon. I go cut down di tall cedars of am, and di choice cypress trees of am. I go enter im farthest height, di forest of im fruitful field.
I don dig and drink water, and with di sole of my feet I go dry up all di rivers of Egypt.’
You no don hear say I don do am long ago, and I don plan am from ancient times? Now I don bring am to pass, say you go lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps.

Dem wey dey live inside dem get little power. Dem dey dismayed and confounded. Dem be like di grass of di field, and like di green herb, like grass on di housetops, and like grain wey dey blasted before e grow.
But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me.
Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance don come up for my ears, I go put my hook for your nose, and my bridle for your lips, and I go turn you back by di way wey you come.”
Dis go be sign to you: you go eat dis year wetin grow by itself, and for di second year wetin spring from am. For di third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards and eat di fruit of dem.
Di remnant wey don escape of di house of Judah go again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.
Because out of Jerusalem go go remnant, and out of Mount Zion dem wey escape. Di zeal of di Lord of Armies go perform dis.
Therefore di Lord talk like dis concerning di king of Assyria: E no go come into dis city, nor shoot arrow dere, nor come before am with shield, nor cast siege mound against am.
By di way wey e come, by di same e go return, and e no go come into dis city, talk di Lord.
Because I go defend dis city to save am, for my own sake, and for di sake of my servant David.’”
Di angel of di Lord go out, and strike for di camp of di Assyrians 185,000. When dem rise up early for morning, see, all dem na dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria depart, and go and return, and live for Nineveh.
As e dey worship for di house of Nisroch im god, Adrammelech and Sharezer im sons strike am with di sword. Dem escape into di land of Ararat. Esarhaddon im son reign for im place.
For dem days Hezekiah dey sick and dey near death. Isaiah di prophet, Amoz pikin, come to am, and talk to am, “Di Lord talk like dis: ‘Set your house in order, because you go die, and no go live.’”
Den Hezekiah turn im face to di wall, and pray to di Lord,
and talk, “Remember now, di Lord, I beg, how I don waka before you in truth and with perfect heart, and don do wetin good for your sight.” Hezekiah cry bitterly.
Den di word of di Lord come to Isaiah, say,
“Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘Di Lord, di God of David your papa, talk like dis: I don hear your prayer. I don see your tears. See, I go add to your days 15 years.
I go deliver you and dis city out of di hand of di king of Assyria, and I go defend dis city.
Dis go be di sign to you from di Lord, say di Lord go do dis thing wey e don speak:
See, I go make di shadow of di steps, wey don go down for di sundial of Ahaz with di sun, return backward ten steps.’” So di sun return ten steps for di sundial wey e don go down.
Di writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when e dey sick and don recover of im sickness.
“I talk, ‘For di middle of my days I must go into di gates of Sheol. Dem don deprive me of di rest of my years.’
I talk, ‘I no go see di Lord, even di Lord for di land of di living. I no go look on man again among di inhabitants of di world.
My dwelling dey plucked up and carried away from me like shepherd tent. I don roll up my life like weaver. E go cut me off from di loom. From day to night you go make end of me.
I wait patiently till morning. Like lion, so e break all my bones. From day to night you go make end of me.
Like swallow or crane, so I chirp. I moan like dove. My eyes fail with looking upward. Lord, I dey oppressed. Be my security.
Wetin I go talk? E don speak to me, and imself don do am. I go waka softly all my years because of di bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by dis things men dey live, and for all of dem na di life of my spirit. So you restore me, and make me live.
See, for peace I get great bitterness, but you don love my soul out of di pit of corruption, because you don cast all my sins behind your back.
Because Sheol no fit praise you. Death no fit celebrate you. Dem wey go down into di pit no fit hope for your truth.
Di living, di living, e dey praise you, as I dey do today. Di papa go make im children know your truth.
Di Lord dey ready to save me. Therefore we go sing my songs with stringed instruments all di days of our life for di house of di Lord.’”
Now Isaiah don talk, “Make dem take lump of figs, and lay am for di boil, so that e go recover.”
Hezekiah too don talk, “Wetin be di sign say I go go up to di house of di Lord?”
Dat time Merodach Baladan, Baladan pikin, king of Babylon, send letters and gift to Hezekiah, because e don hear say e dey sick and don recover.

Hezekiah dey glad because of dem, and show dem di house of im precious things, di silver, di gold, di spices, di precious oil, all im armoury, and all wey dey find for im treasures. Nothing no dey for im house, nor for all im dominion, wey Hezekiah no show dem.
Den Isaiah di prophet come to King Hezekiah, and talk to am, “Wetin dis men talk? And from where dem come to you?” Hezekiah talk, “Dem come from far country to me, from Babylon.”
E talk, “Wetin dem don see for your house?” Hezekiah talk, “All wey dey for my house, dem don see. Nothing no dey among my treasures wey I no show dem.”
Den Isaiah talk to Hezekiah, “Hear di word of di Lord of Armies:
‘See, di days dey come, wey all wey dey for your house, and wey your fathers don store up until dis day, go dey carried to Babylon. Nothing go remain,’ talk di Lord.
‘Dem go take away some of your sons wey go come from you, wey you go father, and dem go be eunuchs for di palace of di king of Babylon.’”
Den Hezekiah talk to Isaiah, “Di word of di Lord wey you don speak good.” E talk dis because e think say, “Peace and truth go dey for my days.”
“Comfort, comfort my people,” talk una God.
“Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry to her say her warfare don finish, say her iniquity don dey pardoned, say she don receive from di Lord hand double for all her sins.”
Di voice of one wey dey cry, “Prepare di way of di Lord for di wilderness. Make straight for di desert highway for our God.
Every valley go dey lifted up, and every mountain and hill go dey made low. Di rough ground go become level, and di rugged places plain.
Di glory of di Lord go dey revealed, and all flesh go see am together, because di mouth of di Lord don speak am.”
Di voice of one wey talk, “Cry!” E talk, “Wetin I go cry?” “All flesh na grass, and all im glory be like di flower of di field.
Di grass dey wither, di flower dey fade, because di breath of di Lord blow on am. Surely di people na grass.
Di grass dey wither, di flower dey fade, but di word of our God go stand forever.”
You wey bring good news to Zion, go up on di high mountain. You wey bring good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength. Lift am up. No fear. Talk to di cities of Judah, “See, your God!”
See, di Lord God go come as mighty one, and im arm go rule for am. See, im reward dey with am, and im recompense before am.
E go feed im flock like shepherd. E go gather di lambs with im arm, and carry dem for im bosom, and go gently lead dem wey dey nursing.
Who don measure di waters for di hollow of im hand, and mark off di sky with span, and enclose di dust of di earth for basket, and weigh di mountains for scales, and di hills for balance?
Who don direct di Spirit of di Lord, or being im counselor don teach am?
Who e take counsel with, and who instruct am, and teach am di path of justice, and teach am knowledge, and show am di way of understanding?
See, di nations dey like drop from bucket, and dem dey regarded as dust on di scales. See, e dey lift up di islands like very small thing.
Lebanon no go dey enough for burning, nor im animals enough for burnt offering.
All di nations dey like nothing before am. Dem dey regarded by am as less than nothing, and emptiness.
To who den una go compare God? Or wetin likeness una go compare to am?
Di craftsman cast idol, and di goldsmith overlay am with gold, and cast silver chains.
Di one wey too poor for such offering choose tree wey no go rot. E seek for imself skilful craftsman to set up idol wey no go move.
Una no know? Una no hear? Dem no tell una from di beginning? Una no understand from di foundations of di earth?
Na im sit above di circle of di earth, and di inhabitants of am dey like grasshoppers. Na im stretch out di heavens like curtain, and spread dem out like tent to dwell in.
Na im bring princes to nothing. E make di judges of di earth like emptiness.
Yes, dem no dey planted. Yes, dem no dey sown. Yes, dem stem no take root for di ground. Even e blow on dem, and dem wither, and di whirlwind carry dem away like stubble.
“To who den una go compare me, so that I go be like am?” talk di Holy One.
Lift up una eyes on high, and see: who don create dis things? Na im bring out dem army by number. E call dem all by name. By di greatness of im might, and im strength of power, no one dey missing.
Why you talk, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way dey hidden from di Lord, and my cause dey disregarded by my God”?
Una no know? Una no hear? Di everlasting God, di Lord, di Creator of di ends of di earth, no dey faint, neither e dey weary. Im understanding no get searching.
E dey give power to di faint, and to dem wey no get might e dey increase strength.
Even di youths go faint and dey weary, and di young men go utterly fall;
but dem wey wait for di Lord go renew dem strength. Dem go mount up with wings like eagles. Dem go run, and no go dey weary. Dem go waka, and no go faint.
